name: German Expressionist cinema
summary: A studio cinema of painted sets, hard single-source light and distorted perspective. The frame shows the mind of the character, not the street. Black-and-white prints are tinted by scene.

philosophy.core_thesis: The set, the light and the body show inner fear, so the picture is built as a state of mind and not recorded as a place.
design_principles: Light each scene with one hard key at a key-to-fill ratio of 8:1 or more, and paint or cast shadows onto walls and floor so that the shadow is a shape in the set.
Build sets with no true right angle: lean walls, doors and stairs 5° to 20° off the vertical, and make doorways taper by 10% to 30%.
Frame in 1.33:1 and place the figure in the lower third, with 50% or more of the frame left to a looming shadow or a steep diagonal.
Cut at an average shot length of 6 to 10 s and hold a silhouette or a stare for 4 s or more before the cut.
Open and close scenes with an iris of 0.5 to 1 s, and use a slow dissolve of 1 to 2 s between a place and a memory.
Tint the print by scene: amber for lit interiors, blue for night, green for the uncanny, and keep each tint for the whole scene.
Direct the actor in held, stylised gesture: 1 to 2 s to a pose, hands and eyes wide, no naturalistic business.
anti_patterns: Location photography of real streets and rooms
Even, soft studio light with fill above 3:1
Straight vertical walls and a level horizon
Rapid cutting under 3 s average shot length
A single neutral grey grade over the whole film

composition.framing: A 1.33:1 frame, tight on the figure, with the set pressing in from the edges.
composition.staging_in_depth: Painted perspective stacks flats at 3 to 5 depths; a shadow or a stair leads the eye from the lit figure to a dark point in the upper third.
composition.subject_placement: Low in the frame, off centre by 15% to 25%, with the looming shape above and behind the figure.

principles.rule: Set one hard key against a near-black set, and let the lit face be the only bright mass in each shot.
Put the lit figure low in the frame and let a looming shadow or stair take the upper third.
principles.value: figure in the lower 33% of the frame

principles.rule: Paint stairs, walls and shadows as diagonals that run from the edge of the frame to the figure.
Stack painted flats at several depths so that perspective is false but deep.
Leave a large dark mass above or beside the figure as the main shape of the frame.
principles.value: 50% or more of the frame dark

camera_and_movement.movement: Mostly locked-off. Where the camera moves, it moves with a purpose: a slow tracking shot toward a face or a dolly through a set.
camera_and_movement.support: Heavy tripod; studio dolly for the rare move
camera_and_movement.camera_height: 0.8 to 1.7 m; low angles under 1 m for a looming figure
camera_and_movement.move_speed: 0.2 to 0.5 m/s for a track or push-in

lens_and_format.frame_rate: 16 to 20 fps capture by hand crank; project at 18 to 20 fps
lens_and_format.aperture: f/4 to f/5.6 for deep focus on the set
lens_and_format.focus: Deep focus on the whole set; a soft iris vignette closes on the face.

light.quality: Hard, from a single arc or tungsten source, with deep cast shadows and painted shadow shapes.
light.direction: Low side or from below on the face; backlight to throw a long shadow up the wall.
light.colour_temperature: Tinted print: amber near 2800K, blue near 8000K for night
light.source: Arc lamps and tungsten on a studio stage

colour_and_grade.treatment: Black and white with a flat tint for each scene. Blacks stay deep, and the highlights carry the tint.
grade_recipe: Convert to black and white and set the black point at 2% and the white point at 94%.
Add a hard S-curve of +35% contrast around mid grey.
Tint by scene with a single-colour wash at 40% to 60% strength: amber hue 35°, blue hue 215°, green hue 100°.
Add film grain at 12% and a 3% to 5% flicker in exposure from frame to frame.
Add a corner iris vignette of −25% and keep it for the iris transitions.
colour_and_grade.texture: Coarse silver grain, amount 12%, with gate weave of 0.5%

editing_and_rhythm.average_shot_length: 6 to 10 s (silent films of the 1920s; check Cinemetrics for each title)
editing_and_rhythm.shot_length_range: 2 s for a shock cut to 25 s for a held stare
editing_and_rhythm.cutting_logic: Cut on the entrance of a shadow or on a gaze. Each scene builds one mood, and the cut serves the scene.
editing_and_rhythm.transitions: Iris in and out (0.5 to 1 s), slow dissolve (1 to 2 s), double exposure for a ghost or a dream.
editing_and_rhythm.runtime: 60 to 110 min in five or six acts

sound.approach: The film is silent. A live orchestra or a piano supplies the sound at the screening.
sound.dialogue: Intertitle cards, 2 to 4 s each, 6 to 12 words.
sound.music: Orchestral score with drones and a leitmotif for the monster; modern releases use a new score.
sound.loudness: None: silent. A new score for a release sits at −23 LUFS.

titles_and_graphics.treatment: Intertitles in jagged, hand-drawn letters that lean and spike like the set.
titles_and_graphics.type: Display face with angular, uneven strokes; white on black; 5% to 10% of letters rotated 3° to 8°.

shot_primer.opening: Open with an iris on a distorted street or a stair; hold the establishing shot for 4 to 6 s.

positive: black and white with amber tint

lineage.root: It is the earliest film style in the data; the silent cinema before 1920 that it came from has no style record yet.

emotion.target_response: Dread and unease: the viewer is inside a mind that the world is bending.

use_cases: horror and thriller titles and trailers
music video with a gothic set
video prompts for a haunted or dream scene
avoid_when: The brief needs a believable, real place or a documentary tone.
The piece must hold the viewer for under 10 s on a feed with a fast cut.

modifiers.how: Keep the hard light and the black and white; leave the studio for a real street, drop the iris and the tint, and shoot handheld at 24 fps.
Keep the 1.33:1 frame and the hard light; cut to an average of 2 to 3 s and join shots by graphic match.

frame_rate.note: A hand crank sets the capture rate.

colour_temperature.note: The value stands for the tint of the print: amber near 2800K, blue near 8000K.
